description: Figure 5(a) is a line plot that displays the training loss curves for different methods during training from scratch. The x-axis, labeled "TFLOPs," represents the number of trillion floating-point operations, with a logarithmic scale ranging from 1e7 to 9e8. The y-axis, labeled "Loss (Value)," represents the training loss value, with a linear scale ranging from 94 to 100. The plot compares five methods: Vanilla (purple), SepLLM (n=64) (orange), SepLLM (n=128) (blue), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red). All methods start with a high loss value, around 98. The Vanilla method shows a rapid decrease in loss, reaching a value of approximately 96.5 by 1e8 TFLOPs. The SepLLM methods generally exhibit a slower decrease in loss compared to Vanilla. The SepLLM (n=64) method starts at a loss of about 97.5 and decreases to around 96.8. The SepLLM (n=128) method starts at a loss of about 97.8 and decreases to around 96.7. The SepLLM (n=64, H) method starts at a loss of about 97.2 and decreases to around 96.6. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) method starts at a loss of about 97.0 and decreases to around 96.5.
